research_question: Owned-page scope: Legal Technology Statistics. Planned sources and method: ABA Legal Technology Survey; separate licensed tools from active users. Build a source-labelled comparison covering legal software adoption and law firm technology spending; record dates, definitions and sample limits. Sources are proposed, not verified findings.

research_brief.purpose: Give law firm leaders a sourced set of legal technology adoption, budgeting, security-policy, and generative AI figures, each tied to the population it describes, and show how to read them without overstating what they prove.
research_brief.audience: Managing partners, operations and IT leads, legal technology buyers, consultants, and researchers who cite legal technology figures.
research_brief.data_period: ABA 2024 Legal Technology Survey Report (release dated March 3, 2025, and the 2024 Budgeting and Planning TechReport); Thomson Reuters publisher summary dated July 2, 2026, covering 2025 and 2026 generative AI use
research_brief.scope_limitations: Desk research from public summaries. The full ABA survey volumes are paid and were not read, so no cross-tabs beyond those in the release and TechReport are used. ABA figures describe different respondent groups (firms, attorneys, litigators). Thomson Reuters figures are organization-level and come from a publisher blog summary. No market-size forecast is quoted because methods are not public.

content_gaps: Ranking pages are either market forecasts with no adoption data or vendor guides that mix populations without saying who was counted.
No reviewed page reports how technology budgeting varies by firm size.
No reviewed page separates adoption, access, active use, spending, and outcomes.
No reviewed page explains why market-size forecasts cannot stand in for adoption rates, or gives an internal audit method.
value_add: Every figure is tied to its population and year, with ABA budgeting data by firm size, security-policy rates, and the 2025 to 2026 change in organizational generative AI use shown in three charts and four tables, plus a five-measure framework and an eight-step internal adoption audit.

drafting_cautions: Keep each ABA percentage attached to firms, attorneys, or litigators as stated
Do not add the two research percentages
Label Thomson Reuters figures as a publisher summary and organization-level
Describe budget findings as percentages of respondents, not dollars
Check before publication whether the ABA has released a newer survey summary

claims.statement: 73% of firms use cloud-based legal tools, 60% have formal cybersecurity policies, 85% of litigators e-file, and 67% and 55% of attorneys use fee-based and free online research.

65.2% of respondents said their firm budgets for technology, 94.1% at firms of 50 to 99 lawyers, 55.4% of solos reported no budget; 53.7% of budgeting firms increased and 23.2% held the budget; 56.8% have an email use policy and 33.9% a personal-device policy.
41% of law firms and 47% of corporate legal departments were using generative AI in 2026, up from 28% and 23% in 2025; 53% of adopters reported seeing a return.
